impl.summary: QMA camera angles (gribbliest's Qwen-Image 2.1 QMA LoRA, 96 views, pinned to 13007eec) are built on the open engine. There is a pure pose-to-view mapper, a validated ComfyUI graph and the model 'QMA · 96 views'. It appears in the Angles app (with an orbit pad), Cinema location views and 3D re-shoots, the turnaround's missing sides plus a new 'Stills · 8 views' route, and the Canvas product-angles template. Research finding: fal now hosts Qwen-Image 2.1 t2i and edit, but with no LoRA input, and Replicate has none. So QMA stays GPU-only and there is no cloud route.

src/lib/qma.ts (pure): vocabulary tables, qmaView(pose) (azimuth snapped to 45° steps, elevation bands at -15/15/45, distance bands at 2.5/7.5), qmaPose (the reverse), qmaPrompt/parseQmaPrompt/qmaRunPrompt, qmaLabel, orbitDrag, QMA_TURN_SET, QMA_MODEL/QMA_WORKFLOW.

Graph qwen-image-21-qma: hand-built from the 2.1 edit graph. Source scaled to about 1 MP (ImageScaleToTotalPixels), QMA LoRA at 1.0, KSampler 30 steps / CFG 3 / euler / simple. Bindings include megapixels (0.6 = preview), cfg, loraStrength and vae. Added to library.spec.mjs, model URL table and model-pins.json. Built, then validated against the live CPU ComfyUI (validated: true); manifest sizes kept and requirements.json updated. It uses the int8 DiT (7.26 GB) and int8 encoder (9.35 GB) like every other Fuobe 2.1 graph; the brief's 14.2/17.5 GB are the bf16 files (verified on HF).

Model oss-qwen-image-21-qma 'QMA · 96 views' (open, edit): controls Angle/Height/Distance using the same params as the Angles app (horizontal_angle, vertical_angle, zoom), plus Size (full / 768 preview) and Decoder. It uses the new promptFormat 'qma': planGeneration writes '<qma> {azimuth} {elevation} {distance} {words}' from the pose, and a prompt that is already a QMA prompt passes unchanged. options.loras ties the model to the LoRA's switch in Settings → Models & licences.

Angles app: new Preset.openAlso routes. presetRoutes appends them on the open engine when the catalog has the model, so QMA becomes a third model pick on your GPU and is absent in the cloud. The app's chips set the pose. New OrbitPad component (drag to orbit and raise, arrow keys, snaps to the nearest view, kept in sync with the chips). The composer hides a model control already set by the app's choices, so QMA's Angle/Height/Distance aren't asked twice.

Cinema: location views take modelId QMA on the open engine. Soul Location gets a 'QMA · 96 views' switch on the open engine. RECOMPOSE_MODELS.open adds QMA, which re-shoots the still from the flown pose snapped to the nearest view.

Turnaround: qmaHorizontal(side). QMA turns the camera, so the person's right side is QMA's 270°. New input fillWith 'qma' (open) draws the missing sides with QMA; the dialog shows a 'Drawn with' choice. New route 'stills' (open, QMA): 7 views at eye level drawn from the front, or chained from a front drawn from the sheet, in one batch with no film. The dialog hides length and shape for it, and shows the pictures and 'ready' when done. The API schema accepts route 'stills' and fillWith.
Canvas product-angles: on the open engine the three angle nodes run QMA with their pose in params.extra. TplNode gets a per-engine 'on' data override. The cloud keeps Nano Banana Pro unchanged.

GPU pre-flight board: STUDIO_ROWS row 'Turnaround stills · 8 views' (/character-sheet?stills=1) → qwen-image-21-qma. The model and the Angles app's QMA route get their chips from the existing model and preset rows.

Qwen-Image 2.1 RGBA note for Layers (not built): the 2.1 VAE decodes four channels (every 2.1 graph ends in SplitImageWithAlpha to drop alpha), and fal's 2.1 says PNG/WebP keep transparency. A Layers route could keep the alpha output by saving before SplitImageWithAlpha. This is untested: alpha quality is unknown.

findings.summary: The Stills · 8 views set names each picture by QMA's camera-relative words, but those names don't match the person's sides. The same package's fill step uses the opposite convention.
findings.detail: planTurnaround's stills branch sends horizontal_angle 90 and titles the result 'Turnaround stills · Right side' (the step label is 'Right side'). The QMA card (read at 13007eec) says 'right side view' means the camera swings 90° to its own right, which shows the person's LEFT side. The implementer's own qmaHorizontal('right') = 270 encodes exactly this, and the fill step labels 'Right side (QMA)' at 270. So inside one turnaround dialog a still called 'Right side' shows the person's left side, while the fill called 'Right side' shows their right. Character Sheet / SIDE_NAMES use the person's sides. Verified with a probe of planTurnaround({engine:'open', route:'stills', views:{front}}): still-90 → 'Right side', still-270 → 'Left side'; the fill run gives fill-right → 270, fill-left → 90.
findings.fix: Label the stills by the person's side (map each azimuth through 360-h, or reuse SIDE_NAMES/qmaHorizontal) and keep the camera's words only in the prompt.

findings.summary: Canvas 'product-angles' on the open engine gives all three angle nodes the same prompt (QMA_STUDIO). Switching that board to the cloud gives Nano Banana Pro three identical prompts with no angle words: three identical shots.
findings.detail: The open variant writes on.open.prompt = 'on a seamless studio background, soft key light, sharp details' for front, side and top, and puts the angle only in params.extra. convertEngine(graph, 'cloud') keeps n.data.prompt and runs sanitizeParams, which deletes params.extra. The probe shows front/side/top → nano-banana-pro, each with the same prompt and params undefined. On the base, the open nodes kept their 'three-quarter front' / 'side profile' / 'top-down' words, so converting kept each shot's meaning. A board started on your GPU and later switched to the cloud now silently loses its three angles.
findings.fix: Keep each node's angle words in the open prompt (QMA tolerates edit words after the camera words). Or have convertEngine / counterpart restore the template's cloud prompt when it leaves QMA.

findings.summary: The finished 'Stills · 8 views' set shows only 7 pictures: the front is missing. They come in reverse order (front-left first, front-right last) and have no side labels.
findings.detail: RunView builds the pictures from state.rows outputs, which hold only the 7 generated turns, in newest-first order. The user's front picture isn't shown, and nothing names each view. Seen in the e2e screenshot stills-done.png at 1440 light. The route and button promise 8 views ('Make 8 views').
findings.fix: Put the front source first, sort by step index, and caption each picture with its side.

findings.summary: The open Canvas template always uses QMA_MODEL, without the offered check the other placements make.
findings.detail: Turnaround (has(QMA_MODEL) through isOffered), Cinema location view (getModel), the Angles app (presetRoutes has()) and Soul Location (getModel) all check that the model is there. tpl() picks QMA unconditionally. When the admin switches the QMA LoRA off in Settings → Models & licences, isOffered is false (recipeLoraOff), yet a new open product-angles board still gets three QMA nodes, and their runs are refused for the switched-off LoRA. The base used oss-qwen-image-21, which isn't tied to that switch. Traced in code, not run.
findings.fix: Fall back to oss-qwen-image-21 (with the old angle prompts) when QMA isn't offered, or resolve template models against the offered catalog.

findings.summary: The GPU board row 'Turnaround stills · 8 views' links to /character-sheet?stills=1, but no page reads 'stills', so the link just opens the Character Sheet.
findings.detail: grep for 'stills' across src/app and src/components finds only the turnaround dialog's route handling. Nothing reads the query param, so the row's link doesn't open the dialog or pre-select the Stills route. It is harmless, but the link promises more than it does.
findings.fix: Either read ?stills=1 on the Character Sheet to open the Turnaround dialog on Stills, or link to plain /character-sheet.

findings.summary: qmaRunPrompt mangles a partial QMA prompt: it strips the trigger and puts the default view's camera words in front, so the camera words conflict.
findings.detail: qmaRunPrompt('<qma> back view', {}) returns '<qma> front-right quarter view eye-level shot medium shot back view' (probe). A user who types a partial QMA prompt directly on the model gets two conflicting azimuths. It could honour the parts given, or at least not leave the stray camera words behind.
findings.fix: Parse a leading partial view (azimuth and optional elevation/distance) and fill only the missing parts from the pose.

findings.summary: On the cloud, nothing tells the user that QMA (Stills · 8 views, Drawn with QMA, Cinema's QMA switch, the Canvas QMA angles) exists on their GPU.
findings.detail: These choices are simply absent on the cloud. The brief asks that 'the cloud engine says plainly that it runs on your GPU (open source)'. The Angles app is covered by the composer's other-engine routes. The turnaround dialog, Cinema's Soul Location and the Canvas template card show nothing on the cloud.
findings.fix: Add a one-line note on the cloud ('8-view stills and QMA angles run on your GPU') where these choices would appear.

fix.finalSummary: Open engine (your ComfyUI): QMA · 96 views runs in the Angles app (with the orbit pad), Cinema location views and 3D re-shoots, the turnaround's missing sides ('Drawn with') and 'Stills · 8 views', and the Canvas product angles. The still set is now named by the person's own sides, the same way the fill step does it. The finished set shows all 8 pictures, front first and captioned. The board link opens the dialog on Stills. Canvas product-angles boards keep each angle's words, so switching a board to the cloud keeps three distinct shots. When the admin switches QMA off, new boards fall back to Qwen-Image 2.1. Verified: the logic in unit tests, the UI in demo mode, and the graph against the CPU ComfyUI (from the implementer's stage). Not verified: picture quality and the camera-relative side convention on a real GPU; the CPU ComfyUI has no weights. That needs the int8 Qwen-Image 2.1 DiT (7.26 GB), the int8 encoder (9.35 GB), the VAE (0.68 GB) and the QMA LoRA (0.32 GB).
